findings.title: Scan staged content before authorizing publication
findings.trigger: An artifact containing sensitive content is staged, then redacted in the working tree without staging the corrected version before the gate runs.
findings.execution_path: The plans stage artifacts before invoking this gate. git ls-files supplies indexed filenames, but grep, awk, and cp all read working-tree contents. Gitleaks scans those working-tree copies. A subsequent ordinary git commit publishes the older indexed content.
findings.consequence: The gate can report PASS while the commit still contains a private path or credential that the gate was intended to block.
findings.evidence: Lines 11–14 enumerate names only; lines 17, 26, and 38 read working files; line 49 copies working files. There is no staged-content extraction or index/worktree equality check. The self-test never stages a sensitive version and then leaves a clean unstaged replacement.
findings.suggested_fix: Scan an immutable snapshot of the index, including the hand-review record, or reject any index/worktree mismatch for covered paths. Add a regression that stages sensitive content, redacts only the working copy, and requires the gate to block.
findings.hypothesis: Static execution-path finding. A disposable Git fixture would demonstrate PASS with sensitive bytes still in the index; creating that fixture was not permitted in this read-only workspace.

findings.title: Preserve the redaction operation when anonymizing the plan
findings.trigger: An executor implements the harness's stdout redaction literally from the revised Step A.
findings.execution_path: The path-anonymization edit changed the source operand of the replacement into '~', leaving the instruction 'replaces ~ with ~'. The resulting operation preserves all input before stream.jsonl is written.
findings.consequence: The prescribed redaction no longer removes private home paths, contradicting the plan's home-path redaction requirement.
findings.evidence: The current instruction explicitly specifies an identity replacement. A synthetic absolute home path remained unchanged when that replacement was applied. The five specified harness self-tests contain no redaction assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe replacing the expanded runtime home directory, such as str(Path.home()), with the literal '~'. Add a synthetic home-path redaction assertion without restoring a personal path to the plan.
findings.reproduction_command: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path(".planning/phases/84-codex-plan-checker-investigation/84-02-PLAN.md"); instruction=p.read_text(); assert "redaction that replaces ~ with ~" in instruction; sample="/Users/example/scratch/planchk-pilot/toy"; actual=sample.replace("~", "~"); assert actual==sample; print("The prescribed replacement preserves the entire private home path.")'
